solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Married woman shows animosity

parts.note: Alice is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A wife displays hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is ill will or a desire to harm, which is a synonym of animosity.

clue.text: Ordered risotto after introduction to Minnie Driver

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged rice dish behind that first letter
introduction to takes the opening letter of Minnie
Ordered means arranged, so the letters of risotto are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Minnie Driver, the actress, ordered risotto after being introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: Minnie Driver is an English actress; 'Driver' is the definition. 'Ordered' rearranges RISOTTO into OTORIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist is someone who drives a car.

clue.text: City thrashed Real, having engaged new players

indicators.note: having engaged means taking on, so the rearranged letters hold the other pieces inside
thrashed suggests the letters of Real are beaten into a new order

parts.note: a cast is the group of players in a show

explanation.surface: A city football side beat Real Madrid after signing fresh players.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a football result, with Real as Real Madrid; 'thrashed' is the anagram signal, and 'having engaged' wraps the jumbled letters round the new players.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster is a historic city in Lancashire, north-west England.

clue.text: Caught university fellows with blow

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
F is the abbreviation for fellow, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Academics were struck when caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuff is a light slap or blow with the hand.

clue.text: One's held back by a stout grating

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: held says the reversed piece is gripped inside the letters of a and stout's synonym
by goes with held: the containing piece is the one doing the holding

parts.note: stout can mean brave or valiant

indicators.note: back tells us the letters for One's are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: One's is I'S, read as I (one) plus S

explanation.surface: Something is restrained by a sturdy metal grille.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' gives IS; 'back' turns it into SI, which is 'held by' A BRAVE. 'Grating' looks like a noun (a grille) but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A grating voice or manner is harsh and irritating, the same as an abrasive one.

clue.text: He will have education to a degree

definitions.text: He will have education to a degree

parts.words: He will have education to a degree
parts.note: to a degree sounds like 'somewhat', but a graduate holding a first degree has this title, and an unmarried man shares the name

explanation.walkthrough: 'To a degree' looks like 'partly' but means up to a university degree; 'He' hints at the unmarried man.
explanation.definitionFit: A holder of a first university degree, such as a BA, is a graduate of that rank; the word also means an unmarried man.

clue.text: Scientist whose study involves moon, star and heart of asteroid?

indicators.note: involves in the sense of entangles, so the letters of these words are mixed together
heart of takes the central letters of asteroid

explanation.surface: An astronomer's work covers moons, stars and asteroids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involves' rearranges MOON and STAR into ASTRONOM; 'heart of' adds ER, the middle two letters of ASTEROID.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomer is a scientist who studies stars, planets and other bodies in space.

clue.text: I am taking a long time to create public persona

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Someone is slowly building up a public profile.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is the impression a person presents to the public.

clue.text: Religious ascetic from German city beginning to evangelise

parts.note: Essen is a city in western Germany

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of evangelise

explanation.surface: A holy hermit sets out from a German city to preach.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an austere Jewish sect around the time of Christ, living lives of self-denial.

clue.text: Frank's lacking a point

definitions.meaning: a knife or pencil lacking a point is not sharp

explanation.surface: A man called Frank is missing the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank's' looks like a man's name with a possessive; it is the adjective plus 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blunt means both bluntly honest in speech and dull-edged, without a sharp tip.

clue.text: Out of gas, grateful for a quantity of it

indicators.note: Out of says a letter is removed, so the synonym for grateful runs short of the gas symbol

parts.note: grateful means thankful
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen, a gas

explanation.surface: A driver who has run dry is thankful to buy fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of' removes H (hydrogen) from THANKFUL. 'It' in the definition points back to 'gas', in the American sense of petrol.
explanation.definitionFit: A tankful is the amount a tank holds, so a tankful of gas is a measured quantity of fuel.

clue.text: Weapon caused injury to young woman

parts.note: to cut someone is to cause them injury
a lass is a young woman

explanation.surface: A weapon was used to hurt a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword once carried by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: One in bar may have one for it?

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for One goes inside the word for bar

parts.note: a rod is a bar of metal or wood
A means one, as in 'a pint'

explanation.surface: A drinker in a pub may have one more before leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'one for the road', a last drink before setting off.
explanation.definitionFit: One for the road is the idiom for a final drink, so the road is what someone may have one for.

clue.text: Woman who suffered capital loss in Lebanon, beaten by fluctuating yen

indicators.note: beaten suggests the letters of Lebanon are knocked about into a new order
fluctuating says the letters of yen shift around too, joining the mix

explanation.surface: Someone lost money in Lebanon as the yen swung about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital loss' sounds financial but means losing one's head. LEBANON plus YEN are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Boleyn, second wife of Henry VIII, was beheaded in 1536, so she lost her head, the capital of the body.

clue.text: Improvised explanation of unfair trial?

definitions.meaning: put together makeshift from what is to hand
a trial where the jurors had been fixed would be explained as one whose jury was rigged

explanation.surface: An improvised excuse for why a court case was unjust.
explanation.definitionFit: Jury-rigged is a nautical term for a makeshift repair; read literally it means a jury tampered with.

clue.text: Start as home counties solicitor

parts.note: the Home Counties, the counties around London, lie in the South East, SE
a tout solicits custom, so is a solicitor in that sense

explanation.surface: A lawyer from the commuter belt begins work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a lawyer but means one who solicits, a tout. The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: To set out is to begin a journey or task, so it can stand for start.

clue.text: Officer without company is beset by depression

indicators.note: is beset by means surrounded, so the word for depression wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a col is a dip or pass between mountain peaks
someone without company is alone, lone

explanation.surface: A lonely officer is gripped by low spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' tempts as gloom but is the geographical sense, a low pass between peaks; 'is beset by' says it surrounds the word for alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior army officer, ranking above a lieutenant colonel.

clue.text: Content of letter must follow quite ridiculous protocol

indicators.note: must follow puts the inner letters of letter after the jumbled piece
ridiculous suggests the letters of quite are made absurd by jumbling them
Content of takes the inside letters of letter, dropping its ends

explanation.surface: What a letter says must observe an absurdly strict code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content of letter' looks like a letter's message but means its inner letters; 'ridiculous' jumbles quite, and 'must follow' sets those inner letters behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette is the code of polite behaviour, a synonym of protocol in its social sense.

clue.text: Company moves fast across lake in rowing boats

indicators.note: across says the word for moves fast stretches over the letter for lake

parts.note: races means moves fast

explanation.surface: A firm speeds over a lake in rowing boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Coracles are small round boats of wicker and hide, paddled in Wales and Ireland.

clue.text: Naturally I must escape from ferocious bats

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the remaining letters are scrambled
must escape from says the letter I leaves the word ferocious

explanation.surface: Someone naturally has to flee vicious flying bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like the animals but means mad. FEROCIOUS less I is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Of course means naturally, as an assent to something obvious.

clue.text: Runs into shy university teacher in London borough

indicators.note: into says the letter for Runs is put inside the word for shy

parts.note: coy means shy or bashful
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a don is a university teacher, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into a timid lecturer in a part of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Croydon is a large borough in south London, one of the capital's thirty-two boroughs.

clue.text: Supply outstanding artwork

definitions.meaning: aid or supplies sent to those in need
a sculpture whose figures stand out from a flat background

explanation.surface: Provide a superb piece of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' seems to mean excellent but literally means standing out from the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief is both aid supplied to the needy and carving raised from a flat background.

clue.text: Timeless longing to find old Chinese text

indicators.note: Timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: itching means longing, eager

explanation.surface: An eternal desire to discover ancient Chinese writings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' means without T (time): ITCHING less T.
explanation.definitionFit: The I Ching, or Book of Changes, is an ancient Chinese book of divination.

clue.text: Rich, even when penniless?

parts.note: without its P, the abbreviation for penny, the word still means rich: LUSH

explanation.surface: Wealthy even when broke?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penniless' means minus P (penny). Take P from the answer and LUSH remains, which also means rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Plush means luxurious and opulent, so it can mean rich in the sense of sumptuous.

clue.text: Generous Alberich awkwardly accepts thanks

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the rearranged name holds the thanks piece inside
awkwardly suggests the letters of the setter's name are put clumsily into a new order

parts.note: ta is an informal British word for thanks

explanation.surface: The setter, rather gauche, receives some gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Alberich is the pen name of this puzzle's setter, so the name is fodder rather than a person; 'awkwardly' jumbles it and 'accepts' takes the thanks inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable means giving freely to others, a synonym of generous.

clue.text: Somewhat irrational loathing for Scottish town

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A slightly unreasonable dislike of a Scottish place.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft definition included 'for', but that is a link word; the town alone is defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a town in Clackmannanshire in central Scotland, on the River Forth.

clue.text: French bread?

parts.note: bread is slang for money, so French bread is the currency used in France

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a baguette, but 'bread' is slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the currency of France, so it is French money, slang 'bread'.

clue.text: A drop in rent

definitions.meaning: a drop of water from the eye

explanation.surface: A fall in what a tenant pays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord but is a rip.
explanation.definitionFit: Tear means a teardrop and, said differently, a rip or rent in cloth.

clue.text: Sick joke finally gets girl banned

parts.note: ill means sick

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of the word joke

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A tasteless joke gets a young woman barred.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illegal is forbidden by law, which is what banned means.

clue.text: Southern climate's not hot — so wear this?

indicators.note: not says the letter for hot is left out of the word for climate

parts.note: weather is taken loosely as climate
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: The south is chilly, so put on a woolly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes H from WEATHER. The definition makes sense with the whole clue: it is cold, so wear this.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweater is a knitted jumper worn for warmth when the weather is cold.

clue.text: Old lady faces adversity, ignoring the odds — most impressive

parts.note: gran, a grandmother, is an old lady

indicators.note: ignoring the odds means skip the first, third and other odd-placed letters of adversity

explanation.surface: An elderly woman confronts hardship against all chances, impressively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faces' only means GRAN comes first. 'Ignoring the odds' sounds like bravery but keeps the even letters of ADVERSITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandest is the superlative of grand, meaning magnificent or imposing.

clue.text: Cheese's said to give one wind

indicators.note: said to give tells us the answer is how the cheese word sounds when spoken

parts.note: Brie's (or bries) is a cheese, said like the answer

explanation.surface: A cheese is claimed to cause flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' here is a gentle breeze, not the digestive sort the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze is a light wind.
